entries.finding: Teaching says the Land Use Act itself fixes 99 years; the Act only requires a definite term
entries.reason: Section 8 of the Act requires a definite term but names no figure; 99 years is the usual maximum in practice and the syllabus answer. Stating it as the Act's own figure is a scoped fact stated as law.
entries.change: Hint 3, principle, How to tell, all three distractor lines and exam tip reworded to teach 99 years as the usual maximum term taught in the syllabus, with the Act requiring a definite term. Key unchanged.

entries.finding: 'removes that dependence' and 'do not change when the crop can be grown' are absolutes
entries.reason: Mulching can stretch the growing period a little, so the C line was too absolute; 'removes' overstated irrigation's effect.
entries.change: How to tell now says irrigation 'directly reduces' the dependence; C line says cultural practices can stretch the season a little but do not supply dry-season water.

entries.finding: A line calls local varieties 'low-yielding' and says research replaces them
entries.reason: Unscoped generalisation; local varieties carry useful traits and are breeding material.
entries.change: A line rewritten: using local varieties as they are does not by itself bring new improvements, though they are often used as parents in breeding.

entries.finding: 'Rocks formed from cooled molten rock do not build up in layers'; 'crystals, not layers'
entries.reason: Lava flows and some igneous bodies are layered; the valid distinction is sedimentary strata.
entries.change: Hint 2 scoped to strata formed by settling; How to tell says strata are not a typical feature of igneous rocks; A, C, D lines reworded to 'settled layers' and D notes lava flows can pile up but are not sedimentary strata.

entries.finding: Exam tip 'check the answer is smaller than both' is false in general
entries.reason: Water lost can exceed the dry soil mass in a very wet sample; only the fresh mass is a true upper bound.
entries.change: Exam tip now checks against the fresh soil mass only.

entries.finding: 'A practice that adds any of these cannot prevent pollution'; 'keeps synthetic chemicals off the farm'; 'removes them'
entries.reason: Absolutes; pollution depends on amounts reaching water, and organic manure can also pollute if mismanaged.
entries.change: Hint 2 now asks for the practice that cuts down these sources; How to tell says organic farming avoids synthetic fertilizers and pesticides and a preventive practice cuts down a source; exam tip reworded to 'cuts down'. Codex's proposed C line and principle rewrite not applied: the existing wording was already correct.

entries.finding: Hint 3 'leaves make food rather than store it' is unscoped
entries.reason: Some leaves store food; the valid point is that the yam's food store is not its leaves.
entries.change: Hint 3 and the D distractor line now say yam leaves are not where the yam keeps its food store.

entries.finding: 'Nematodes live in the soil and attack roots'; 'Neither depends on how wet the harvested grain is'
entries.reason: Some nematodes attack seeds and above-ground parts; the claim needs syllabus scoping.
entries.change: Hint 2 and A line scoped with 'in the syllabus ... treated mainly as' root pests; hint 2 now says neither is the usual cause of spoilage in damp grain.

entries.finding: Protein loss overstated; germ removal and 'cannot sprout' stated absolutely
entries.reason: Most rice protein stays in the endosperm, and polishing removes most but not always all of the germ.
entries.change: Hint 2 and principle say 'most of the germ'; principle lists 'some of its protein'; D line says polished rice sprouts poorly, if at all.

entries.finding: Phytophthora called a true fungus without scoping
entries.reason: Phytophthora is a fungus-like oomycete; the syllabus groups gummosis with fungal diseases, so one qualifier is needed.
entries.change: Principle: 'Phytophthora, a soil-borne organism that the syllabus groups with the fungi'. Hint 2 now says 'soil-borne disease'.

entries.finding: 'a nitrogen-fixing tree must be a legume' is a false absolute
entries.reason: Casuarina and other non-legumes fix nitrogen with Frankia.
entries.change: How to tell now says Leucaena is the only legume among the options and the standard syllabus example; exam tip changed to 'usually points to a legume' for the same reason (self-applied check 11).

entries.finding: Hint 3 'bushy flowering plant used in hedges' hands over shrub
entries.reason: 'Bushy' plus 'hedges' is the definition of shrub, so hint 3 answers the question without recall.
entries.change: Hint 3 now asks the student to compare Allamanda's height and stem arrangement with the two forms.

entries.finding: Keteku is an N'Dama x zebu cross, not Muturu x zebu
entries.reason: Accepted in part. Sources differ: Keteku (Borgu) is recorded as a cross of West African humpless shorthorn cattle (the Muturu/Somba type) with zebu, and some texts give N'Dama. Codex's claim that Muturu has no part in its ancestry is not established either, so naming a single parent breed risks a wrong fact.
entries.change: Hint 3 calls Keteku 'a crossbred breed'; B line says 'a cross between humpless West African cattle and zebu cattle'.

entries.finding: Hint 3 gives the 180 m² area and the exact division
entries.reason: Handing over the area, which is distractor C, plus the operation leaves nothing to set up.
entries.change: Hint 3 no longer states the area; it tells the student to divide their area by 0.36 m² and offers the ×100 trick for the sum.

entries.finding: 'Only sheep grow wool'; goats and rabbits called hair or fur
entries.reason: Angora goats and rabbits give wool-type fibre; the sheep link is a syllabus convention.
entries.change: Hint 2, principle and How to tell scoped with 'in the syllabus'; B line says the syllabus links wool with sheep.

entries.finding: Hint 2 eliminates maize, yam and plantain by name, leaving the answer
entries.reason: Eliminating all three distractors in hint 2 states the answer indirectly.
entries.change: Hint 2 now gives the principle (export cash crops versus staples) without naming options.

entries.finding: Difficulty easy should be medium
entries.reason: A single division with a figure given in the passage is not clearly wrong as easy, and it matches Q11 and Q48 which are the same size of step; the standard says change difficulty only if clearly wrong.

entries.finding: '1/100 × 500' is ASCII-style notation
entries.reason: Unicode notation is the standard; ÷ reads more clearly.
entries.change: Working line now reads 'Family use = 1% of 500 = 500 ÷ 100 = 5 trays'.

entries.finding: Difficulty easy should be medium
entries.reason: 1% of 500 then a subtraction is a one-step calculation; easy is not clearly wrong.

entries.finding: Hint 2 states valuation at full cost as a general farm-accounting rule
entries.reason: Valuing home use at full cost is this question's method, not a universal rule; the solution already scoped it.
entries.change: Hint 2 now says 'For this question, value those trays at the full cost of each tray'.

entries.finding: 'Advertisement raises demand', 'keeps longer and sells for more', 'raise demand and so the price' stated as automatic
entries.reason: Each is a possible effect, not a guaranteed one.
entries.change: Hint 3, principle, How to tell and C line softened to 'can'; C line now says advertisement can raise demand and so support a better price.

entries.finding: Siblings Q11 to Q13 (shared soil results) read together
entries.reason: No hint gives away a sibling's answer: Q11 hints find fresh soil only, Q12 hints find water lost only, Q13 hints set up the ratio without stating either earlier figure.

entries.finding: Siblings Q47 to Q49 (egg farm passage) read together
entries.reason: Q47 hints name only the production cost; Q48 hints work only trays sold; Q49 hints come after both are answered. No leak.

entries.finding: Q23 shares a stem with Q21 and Q22, which are not in this batch
entries.reason: Q23 hints speak of damp grain and moulds and do not name the illustrated crop, so they do not answer an identify-the-crop sibling.

entries.finding: hint 3 too strong: 'which one adds a chemical ... and which one avoids it'
entries.reason: Hint 3 is meant to narrow to two, and it does; the student must still know that herbicide is a synthetic chemical and that organic farming avoids such chemicals, which is the fact the question tests. The proposed fix names both options and adds the absolute 'using only natural methods', so it is no weaker and less accurate.

entries.finding: hint 3 matches each of I, II, III to the hint 2 test for the student
entries.reason: Hint 3 states for every numeral that it meets the price-raising test from hint 2 ('Advertisement can raise demand, grading sorts produce by quality, and processing can add value'), so a student can pick D without judging any function.
entries.change: Replaced hint 3 with Codex's version, which asks the student to test each function against hint 2 without stating the result.

entries.finding: checked for unscoped absolutes
entries.reason: Claims are hedged ('greatly reduces', 'can poison', 'can run off'); nothing needs scoping.

entries.finding: checked for unscoped absolutes
entries.reason: Claims use 'can' and 'several of them'; nothing needs scoping.
